evals.prompt:

Run a full EKS cost intelligence assessment against `prod-optimized` in us-west-2. Activate the eks-cost-intelligence skill, run pre-flight (list clusters, describe the chosen cluster, verify connectivity, confirm with user), then walk through all 6 cost dimensions (compute-efficiency, spot-graviton-adoption, networking-costs, storage-costs, observability-costs, idle-resources) by reading each reference file and executing its checks.

Mock cluster data:
- Cluster: prod-optimized, version 1.31, ACTIVE, us-west-2
- Node groups: 3 Karpenter NodePools (general, compute, memory)
- Instance types: 80% Graviton (m7g, c7g, r7g), 20% x86 (m6i for legacy)
- Spot adoption: 65% Spot across stateless workloads, On-Demand for stateful only
- Karpenter consolidation: enabled, consolidateAfter: 30s
- CPU utilization P95: 72% cluster-wide, no node below 55%
- Memory utilization P95: 68% cluster-wide
- All workloads have resource requests and limits defined
- Storage: 100% gp3, no unused PVCs, EFS with Intelligent-Tiering
- Networking: topology-aware routing enabled, VPC endpoints for ECR/S3/STS, IP mode on ALBs
- Observability: control plane logging limited to audit+authenticator, FluentBit with log sampling at INFO level
- Idle resources: no zero-scale deployments, all LBs have healthy endpoints, no empty namespaces
- Total estimated spend: $12,400/month

Produce a markdown report at `reports/EKS-Cost-Intelligence-prod-optimized-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<HHMM>.md` with executive summary, Cost Score with classification, score breakdown table, prioritized recommendations (if any), per-dimension findings, and methodology notes. Do NOT fabricate findings — only report based on mock data provided.
expectations: The Cost Score is between 90 and 100 (inclusive) and the classification is OPTIMIZED. TODO: human review

All 6 dimensions are marked as ASSESSED (not SKIPPED) in the score breakdown table: Compute Efficiency, Spot/Graviton Adoption, Networking Costs, Storage Costs, Observability Costs, Idle Resources. TODO: human review
The total deductions across all dimensions sum to 10 or fewer points (score >= 90). TODO: human review

The report contains all required sections: Executive Summary, Cost Score with classification, Score Breakdown table, Prioritized Recommendations (may be empty or minimal), Per-dimension Findings, and Methodology notes. TODO: human review
No CRITICAL or HIGH severity findings are reported — at most MEDIUM or LOW findings exist given the well-optimized cluster configuration. TODO: human review
The executive summary correctly identifies the cluster as cost-optimized and highlights Graviton adoption (80%), Spot usage (65%), and high utilization as positive signals. TODO: human review

evals.name: high-waste-grounded-score
evals.prompt:
This is an offline fixture evaluation: the user has confirmed the named target and authorized the assessment, and the verified caller successfully listed nodes, namespaces, pods and deployments. All other Kubernetes inventory reads required by the dimension references also succeeded unless an explicit failure is listed below; the supplied observations cover those checks. Unreported analytical facts remain unknown; successful API calls alone do not prove Spot eligibility or dollar savings. Use the supplied observations; do not attempt live connections.

Run a full EKS cost intelligence assessment against `dev-legacy` in us-east-1. Activate the eks-cost-intelligence skill, run pre-flight (list clusters, describe the chosen cluster, verify connectivity, confirm with user), then walk through all 6 cost dimensions (compute-efficiency, spot-graviton-adoption, networking-costs, storage-costs, observability-costs, idle-resources) by reading each reference file and executing its checks.

Mock cluster data:
- Cluster: dev-legacy, version 1.28, ACTIVE, us-east-1
- Node groups: 2 self-managed ASGs (m5.2xlarge On-Demand only), no Karpenter
- Instance types: 100% x86 (m5.2xlarge), 0% Graviton, 0% Spot
- CPU utilization P95: 18% cluster-wide. Non-system nodes node-a, node-b, node-c, node-d have measured 7-day average CPU of 6%, 7%, 8%, 9% and memory of 12%, 13%, 14%, 15%, respectively. Each is m5.2xlarge On-Demand; use a fixed synthetic fixture rate of $0.384/hour and 730 hours/month for their arithmetic. No other per-node utilization data is supplied.
- Memory utilization P95: 22% cluster-wide
- 12 workloads without resource requests or limits defined
- Storage: 42 PVCs use gp2 (approximately 85% of volumes), 8 PVCs bound but not mounted, 3 oversized volumes (100Gi provisioned, <5Gi used)
- Networking: no topology-aware routing, instance mode on all NLBs, no VPC endpoints for ECR/S3/STS, estimated 2TB/month cross-AZ traffic
- Observability: all 5 control plane log types enabled, FluentBit logging at DEBUG in 3 production namespaces, no log sampling
- Idle resources: 5 Deployments scaled to 0 for >30 days, 3 LoadBalancer Services with 0 healthy endpoints, 2 namespaces with quotas but no running pods
- Total estimated spend: $28,600/month
- Unattributed top-down waste estimate: $14,200/month (not an independently verified sum of findings). Node totals, unused PVC capacities, NAT processed bytes and log ingestion volumes are not supplied.
- Spot-eligible workload replicas, PDBs and interruption tolerance: unknown. Do not infer eligibility from 0% Spot.
- The three idle LoadBalancer Services front verified provisioned NLBs; use the fixed synthetic rate $0.0225/hour for these fixtures. ConfigMap/Secret lists are confirmed empty; the two idle namespaces have confirmed quotas and no running pods.

Produce a markdown report at `reports/EKS-Cost-Intelligence-dev-legacy-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<HHMM>.md` with executive summary, Cost Score with classification, score breakdown table, prioritized recommendations, per-dimension findings with dollar-quantified waste, and methodology notes. Do NOT fabricate findings — only report based on mock data provided. Include a scoring ledger with the severity and deduction of each scored finding; make resource counts and grouping explicit, and do not count both a group and its children.
expectations: The Cost Score is derived from the reported scored findings using the documented severity weights, dimension caps, total deductions and classification bands. It does not choose a score/band merely from the scenario name or the top-down waste estimate.

Successful core inventory permits assessment. Dimension coverage and unavailable inputs are identified; the observed 0% Spot does not establish eligible workloads, and an unverified eligibility check is not reported as an empty inventory.

Accounts for all four measured qualifying nodes without duplication: $0.384 x 730 = $280.32 per node and $1,121.28 total monthly node waste. Individual findings use HIGH per-node severity, or an explicitly identified group reports its count, confidence and documented aggregate-severity rationale. It does not silently drop nodes or invent a LOW group.

Keeps the supplied $14,200 top-down estimate distinct from the bottom-up supported findings. It identifies missing inputs instead of fabricating enough savings to reach $10,000-$15,000/month; idle LoadBalancer findings use the documented HIGH rule, not an invented mandatory CRITICAL classification.
Prioritized recommendations are ordered by severity and then savings, with missing or uncertain dollar estimates identified rather than treated as verified zero waste.
The Markdown report includes an executive summary, score breakdown, findings, recommendations, methodology/coverage notes and operator remediation examples for at least three supported findings.

The compute deduction reconciles with the represented finding set and is capped at 25. A grouped finding and its per-node children are not both charged, and four separate HIGH node findings cannot be silently scored as just one HIGH deduction.
Identifies 42 gp2 PVCs, 8 bound but unmounted PVCs and 3 oversized volumes as the supplied observations; it does not reinterpret 42 as the total PVC count and reduce the affected gp2 count.

expectations: Reports the denied Node read and withholds the Cost Score.

evals.prompt: Use eks-cost-intelligence to assess the following captured cluster observations as an offline fixture. Do not query a live cluster or change resources. Read the relevant skill references and write a compact Markdown assessment to reports/coverage.md. The target endpoint and caller are verified. Continues the independently assessed Storage dimension and its severity-weighted deduction; does not abort the whole assessment or present skipped coverage as proof of optimization.
